<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>## Verdict

The fix is one level too shallow, and the file's own history proves it: `remote_topology.go` is 5 weeks old and this is the **third** rewrite of the same paragraph for the same reason. `a3136178c` wrote it, `6fe608f93` rewrote it ("stop the destination note contradicting the election"), and this rewrites the failure half. `6fe608f93`'s message even names the right answer and declines to take it: *"It now states the election and points at `entire status`, which already reports the elected destination and the unpushed count, rather than restating precedence rules that would go stale again."* Pointing at status instead of using it is exactly what produced the bug under review. The current change repeats the choice.

That said, several individual decisions inside the change are right (the typed error especially), and the `enable` call site is defensible. Findings below, ordered by depth.

---

### 1. `cmd/entire/cli/remote_topology.go:111` — the resolver is asked, then its answer is thrown away

`if _, err := strategy.ResolveCheckpointSyncRemote(ctx); err != nil` keeps only the error. The success branch at **lines 261–267** still narrates the election from static text ("Checkpoints sync to a single elected remote — not to whichever one you push to… Run `entire status` to see the elected destination") while `inspectRemoteTopology` has the elected name and `Source` in hand and discards both.

So the root cause — *this note asserts what the election decided instead of asking it* — is fixed for the error arm only. The success arm is still a hand-maintained restatement of a five-tier precedence rule, and still sends the user to a second command to learn an answer doctor already computed one function earlier.

**Instead:** bind the whole `CheckpointSyncRemote` into `remoteTopology`, not just `err`, and print it: `Checkpoints sync to "origin" (set by checkpoint_push_remote).` A sentence that names the resolver's own output cannot go stale when a tier is added or `observed` is renamed; a sentence describing the rules can, and has, twice.

### 2. `remote_topology.go:56–66` vs `status.go:330–353` — a second reporter of a condition that already has a single-source-of-truth type, **in the same Go package**

`checkpointSyncInfo` exists, by its own doc comment, as *"the single shared computation behind both the text and JSON checkpoint-sync sections… so the two outputs cannot drift"*, and its `Err` field (`status.go:342`, set at `status.go:366`) is precisely the fail-closed message this change re-derives. Both files are `package cli`; `computeCheckpointSyncInfo(ctx, s)` needs nothing but settings. **The coupling cost of "doctor renders status's computation" is a `settings.Load` call** — there is no package boundary, no import, no cycle.

Weighed seriously, the objection I'd expect (status is a hot path; merging fan-out detection into it adds `git remote -v` + N `PushURL` probes to every `entire status`) argues for merging in *one* direction only: doctor/enable consume `checkpointSyncInfo`, `remoteTopology` stays the doctor-side fan-out input. That costs status nothing and removes the second reporter.

**Instead:** make `checkpointSyncInfo` the one checkpoint-destination verdict, give it the fan-out/other-remote fields, and add a third renderer for the note. Then `status --json`, `status` text, doctor and enable cannot disagree by construction — which is the property the type was created for and which this change quietly breaks.

### 3. `remote_topology.go:157–173` (`syncDisabled`) vs `status.go:362–366` — the pinned exemption is the pre-push gate's policy, re-derived in a renderer, and it now disagrees with the other renderer

Three spellings of one rule are now live:

| site | predicate |
|---|---|
| pre-push gate (`manual_commit_push.go:99`) | `!ps.hasCheckpointURL()` — after a dialing `resolvePushSettings` |
| `status.go:381` | `PushURL(ctx, elected.Name)` — needs an elected remote |
| `remote_topology.go:99` + `168` | `PushURL(ctx, name)` per remote — needs none |

On the same repo (dedicated `checkpoint_remote` + broken `checkpoint_push_remote`), `entire status` prints `! Checkpoints NOT syncing: …` and `entire doctor` prints **nothing**. status.go:362–365 documents its side as an *"Accepted divergence"* from the gate because *"there is no elected remote left to probe PushURL against here"* — and the new code demonstrates that premise was wrong; probing per-remote needs no election. So the change found the better answer and then left it in one command's presentation layer while the other keeps shipping the acknowledged-wrong one.

Two commands disagreeing about "is my session history syncing" is not acceptable divergence — a user who runs both cannot tell which is true.

**Instead:** extract the local half of the gate's exemption once — `remote.DedicatedCheckpointPushCovers(ctx, remoteName) bool`, which is just `GetCheckpointRemote() != nil && PushURL(name).enabled` — and have the gate, `computeCheckpointSyncInfo` and the note all call it. That retires status's accepted divergence rather than institutionalising a second, opposite one.

### 4. `strategy/manual_commit_push.go:99–105` + `checkpoint_sync_remote.go:153`, `:186` — the silence the user actually experiences is at **push time**, and it is untouched

`checkpointSyncAllowedForRemote` logs the fail-closed error at `Warn` into `.entire/logs` (`:153`), and `hintGatedCheckpointSync` returns early on `err != nil` (`:186`, with the comment noting the gate "logs a warning" — to a file). So at the exact moment a `git push` silently drops every checkpoint, the user sees nothing on stderr. This change adds the report to two commands the user must think to run, neither of which they will run *because* the failure is silent.

Crucially, the conditionality that makes the ordinary gated-sync hint hard (habitual destination vs. one-off `git push heroku`, `checkpoint_sync_remote.go:189–204`) **does not apply here**: a `checkpoint_push_remote` naming a non-existent remote is wrong for every push target, so the advice is unconditionally correct. This is the cheapest and highest-yield report of the three, and it is the one not written.

**Instead:** in `hintGatedCheckpointSync`, split the `err != nil` early return — `errors.As` the new `CheckpointPushRemoteNotConfiguredError` and print it to the `stderrWriter` the file already holds.

### 5. `remote_topology.go:285–292` + `setup.go:1434–1441` — `checkpointNoteHeaders` shares the body and parameterises only the register

The struct exists because `enable` wants "Note: checkpoint sync is currently disabled in this repo." and doctor wants "Checkpoint sync: DISABLED" — but everything after the header (`Affected remotes:`, `Fix:`, the `settings.local.json` paragraph) is doctor's voice, printed verbatim under enable's note heading. A two-string struct passed through two functions is the smallest possible way of saying *these are two reports*.

This one is a judgment call and the current form is defensible — it's not a strategy pattern, it's two strings. But it's the seam that grows a third field the first time a caller wants different body wording, and it only exists because the data isn't shared (finding #2).

**Instead:** share the verdict, not the prose. `enable` prints one line; doctor prints the diagnosis block. `checkpointNoteHeaders` then has nothing to do.

### 6. `doctor.go:172–177` — it *is* a doctor check; it just doesn't say so

Everything adjacent (`checkGitHookSymlinks`, `checkEntireDirSymlinks:710`, `checkLogSink:1227`, `checkRetiredDenyRule:1294`) is `func check*(cmd *cobra.Command)` printing `"<Subject>: <STATE>"` + indented remedy. The new output is character-for-character that shape — `Checkpoint sync: DISABLED`, indented cause, `Fix:` — but is reached through a shared helper with its headings inlined at the call site.

The `ambiguous` half genuinely isn't a check (nothing is broken; it's advisory, and shared with `enable` on purpose). The `disabled` half is: it's a misconfiguration with a remedy, i.e. the same class as every `check*` above it. Note also that doctor's `Long` enumerates "Checks performed: 1–5" and this verdict is in none of them — tolerable for a note, less so for a DISABLED finding.

**Instead:** `checkCheckpointSyncDestination(cmd)` beside the others, calling the shared verdict from #2, with its headings as its own constants. `enable` keeps its one-liner. That also deletes the reason `checkpointNoteHeaders` exists.

### 7. `setup.go:1428`, `:1449` — `enable` acquired the new verdict by inheritance, not by decision

The diff adds no call site; it changes an argument, and the disabled report rides along into two flows (`runEnableInteractive`, and `printEnabledStatus`, itself reached from `setup.go:1235` and `:1495`). That's not scope creep in the usual sense — it's the opposite risk: a new verdict appeared in another command's output without anyone choosing it, which is the same failure mode as promoting a command into `agent-help`'s listing by accident.

It happens to be the right outcome. A committed `checkpoint_push_remote` naming a remote this clone lacks is *specifically* a clone-time condition — the change's own remedy text says so ("a committed one disables checkpoint sync in every clone that lacks that name") — and `enable` is when a fresh clone first runs. **Keep it**, but print enable's one-liner rather than doctor's diagnosis block (#5), and say in the PR that it was chosen rather than inherited.

### 8. `strategy/checkpoint_sync_remote.go:43–64` — the typed error is at the right altitude (positive), but it now has two phrasings

The gate is running. Here's the outcome of the four reviews.

## Applied

All four agents converged on one spot — `describeSyncDisabled`'s two `Fix:` branches. Collapsing them (the branches were the same two clauses reordered) deleted the branch, the three-line comment that existed only to explain the branch's deixis, *and* the duplicate `unpinnedNames()` walk that three separate agents flagged. One fix, four findings.

| Fix | Raised by |
|---|---|
| Collapsed the `Fix:` branches → also killed the duplicate `unpinnedNames()` call and its explanatory comment | all four |
| `_, t.electionErr = Resolve…` — the `if err != nil` guard assigned what was already the zero value | simplification |
| `doctorCheckpointNoteHeaders` package var; `doctor.go` and the test now share it | simplification, reuse |
| `describe` → `describeTopology` (generic name in a 172-file shared test package) | reuse |
| Trimmed the bug anecdote from two test comments — it's told in full on the `electionErr` field | simplification |
| Added the remoteless-topology test; `syncDisabled`'s other disjunct had no coverage | simplification |
| Trimmed the integration assertions to what only a real repo proves (wiring + the name's round trip) | simplification |

The test-header copy was the one worth having caught: the test file asserted on its *own* copy of doctor's headings while claiming to assert "the text a user actually sees" — renaming the heading in `doctor.go` would have left all five tests green.

## Skipped

Two agents reached opposite conclusions on the biggest question — whether this should render `status.go`'s `checkpointSyncInfo` instead of being a second reporter. I went with reuse's, having checked it myself: `Err` there is a `string`, so `errors.As` is impossible without rippling into `statusJSON`, and `computeCheckpointSyncInfo` also counts unpushed checkpoints and probes `InheritedCheckpointRemote` — work the note doesn't need. The single source of truth is already `strategy.ResolveCheckpointSyncRemote`; both renderers call it.

Efficiency measured the new resolver call as **zero extra subprocesses** (`WithGitRemoteCache` on the root context memoizes it, and both call sites resolve the election earlier in the same command), ~0.2ms against a function that already spawns three git processes. No finding.

Three altitude findings I'm skipping as out of scope but passing on, since they're real:

1. **The success arm still narrates precedence rules** rather than printing the elected remote it now has in hand — which is why this paragraph has been rewritten three times in five weeks for the same reason. Naming the remote inline would end that. It changes unchanged output and an existing integration assertion, so it's a deliberate product edit, not cleanup.
2. **`hintGatedCheckpointSync` still says nothing on stderr at push time**, which is the moment the data is actually dropped. Both commands I fixed require the user to think to run them. Cheapest, highest-yield follow-up — and unlike the ordinary gated-sync hint, the advice here is unconditionally correct, since a missing remote is wrong for every push target.
3. **The `status`/`doctor` disagreement in dedicated-`checkpoint_remote` mode** — the one I flagged to you earlier. Altitude's angle sharpens it: `status`'s "accepted divergence" is documented on the premise that there's no elected remote left to probe, and this change demonstrates that premise is wrong (probing per-remote needs no election). Worth retiring rather than institutionalising.

I'll confirm when the gate finishes. Still nothing committed.

The checkpoint-destination note narrated the election's rules from static text instead of asking the election what it decided, so a repo whose `checkpoint_push_remote` names a missing remote — where the resolver fails closed and checkpoints sync nowhere — was told they "sync to a single elected remote" and to run `entire status` to see which one. ## The bug

`entire doctor` printed this for a repo whose checkpoint sync election had **failed closed** — `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote` naming a remote that does not exist, so no push carries checkpoint data at all:

```
Checkpoint destination: REVIEW
  This repo has 2 remotes (origin, publish).
    Checkpoints sync to a single elected remote — not to whichever one you
    push to. A push to any other remote carries your code but no session
    history. Run `entire status` to see the elected destination and how many
    checkpoints are waiting for it.
```

There is no elected destination, and `entire status` says `! Checkpoints NOT syncing`.

**A second half, which is worse:** the note fires only on *ambiguity* (>1 unpinned remote, or a fan-out remote). In the ordinary one-remote repo with the same typo, `entire doctor` said **nothing at all** about sync being off.

The cause is that `remote_topology.go` inspects remotes and settings but never calls `strategy.ResolveCheckpointSyncRemote` — it states the election's rules rather than its verdict. That is the same defect the note was already fixed for once: `TestMultiPushURL_DestinationNoteSurfaces` pins that it no longer claims checkpoints "follow whichever remote you push to".

## The fix

`remoteTopology` now consults the resolver, for the same reason `pinned` already asks it rather than reading settings. When the election has failed closed it reports that instead of the destination narration, and it reports regardless of ambiguity, which closes the silent one-remote case. The two conditions are exclusive: while sync is off there is no destination to describe, and the ambiguity paragraphs all narrate where checkpoints land.

```
Checkpoint sync: DISABLED
  checkpoint_push_remote names "gone", which is not one of this repo's remotes,
  so nothing is elected to carry checkpoints.
  Affected remotes: origin, publish
  Pushes to them carry your code but no session history, which stays in
  this clone.
  Fix: remove strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote to let Entire elect one,
  or point it at a remote this repo actually has.
  A remote name is a per-clone fact: prefer .entire/settings.local.json, since a
  committed one disables checkpoint sync in every clone that lacks that name.
```

The `settings.local.json` line is deliberate. A committed `checkpoint_push_remote` fail-closing for a teammate whose clone lacks that remote name is the most likely way this reaches a user, and `hintGatedCheckpointSync` already makes the same argument for the same reason.

The fail-closed return becomes `CheckpointPushRemoteNotConfiguredError` (typed, matched with `errors.As`; message byte-identical, so `entire status` output is unchanged). It exists so a caller can tell the misconfigured setting from the *other* fail-closed outcome — an unreadable settings file — and attach the remedy that fits. An unmatched cause gets no remedy, per the rule the `.entire` directory errors follow.

A remote pinned to a dedicated `checkpoint_remote` URL is exempt from the whole report, because the pre-push gate exempts it from the election (`ps.hasCheckpointURL()`) before consulting it, so its checkpoints really do still ship.

## Two calls a reviewer should make rather than inherit

**`entire enable` gained this report, not just the correction.** Fixing the false paragraph in the shared note was unavoidable for both callers; printing the *disabled* block on enable is an addition beyond the reported defect. It seemed right — a committed setting naming a remote this clone lacks is specifically a clone-time condition, which is exactly when `enable` runs — but it is one paragraph of new output on another command, and easy to scope back to doctor-only.

**`status` and `doctor` now disagree in dedicated-`checkpoint_remote` mode.** `status` warns there anyway, under a documented "Accepted divergence" whose stated premise is that "there is no elected remote left to probe `PushURL` against". This change shows that premise is false: probing per-remote needs no election. I left `status` alone because changing it is a product call, but the divergence looks retirable rather than inherent, and two commands disagreeing about "is my session history syncing" is not a great place to leave it.

## Tests

Six unit tests in a new `remote_topology_test.go` (the file had none), each asserting the **false** phrasings are absent rather than only that the new text is present, plus a coverage case for the remoteless branch. Mutation-checked: forcing `syncDisabled()` true fails three of them, so they are not vacuous. `TestCheckpointSyncRemote_MisconfiguredSettingFailsClosed` — which already builds exactly this repo on both backends — gains the wiring assertion that only a real repo can make.

`mise run check` passes (fmt, lint 0 issues, unit + integration + Vogon canary), plus `GOOS=windows go vet ./...`.

## Follow-ups, deliberately not in scope

- **The success arm still restates precedence rules** instead of printing the elected remote the topology now has in hand. `git log` shows this paragraph rewritten three times in five weeks, each time because a hand-maintained restatement went stale — and the previous rewrite's message explicitly considered using the resolver's answer and chose to point at `entire status` instead, which is what produced this bug. Naming the remote inline would end the cycle, but it changes output outside this defect and an existing integration assertion.
- **`hintGatedCheckpointSync` still says nothing on stderr at push time**, which is the moment the data is actually dropped; both commands fixed here require the user to think to run them. Unlike the ordinary gated-sync hint, the advice is unconditionally correct in this case, since a missing remote is wrong for every push target.
